newsitem.title: USA: Haitian former police chief indicted in Miami.
newsitem.headline: Haitian former police chief indicted in Miami.

text.p: The U.S. Attorney's Office on Friday indicted the feared former police chief of Port-au-Prince, Lieutenant Colonel Joseph Michel Francois, on drug smuggling charges.

The indictment said Francois placed the political and military heirarchy of Haiti's former military goverment under his control in league with Colombian cartels to ship huge quantities of heroin and cocaine into the United States.
Francois, who fled Haiti in 1994, was under arrest and would be brought to Miami to face charges, law enforcement sources said.
He is thought to have been the mastermind behind the September 1991 coup that toppled Haitian President Jean-Bertrand Aristide.
He fled to the Dominican Republic in 1994 after U.S. troops invaded the Caribbean island to restore Aristide to power. He later moved to Honduras, where, the sources said, he was arrested.

In Port-au-Prince, Haitian justice officials said they would seek Francois' return to face charges of murder and other human rights abuses. "We will seek his extradition," said Justice Ministry advisor Jerome Jean Noel. "This is a person that Haitian justice has been looking for for quite some time."
